# Sheet template (optional)

Strecke reads any Google Sheet that has a column named `word` (or `Wort`) and a meaning column. This template is only a convenience: it has every column the app understands, a note on each header, dropdowns for the fixed lists, one example row, and the optional *Inbox* and *Meta* tabs. Column rules: [SHEET_SCHEMA.md](../SHEET_SCHEMA.md).

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `strecke-template.xlsx` | All four tabs in one file: *Read me*, *Words*, *Inbox*, *Meta* |
| `Words.csv`, `Inbox.csv`, `Meta.csv`, `Read-me.csv` | The same tabs as separate CSV files, for importing one at a time |

The files are generated by `python tools/template/make_template.py` (byte-identical on every run) and checked by `core/test/template.test.ts`: every header maps to a known column and the example row reads without a single note. They contain one synthetic example row and nothing else.

Neither the app nor this repository creates anything in anyone's Google Drive. You make your own copy.

## Make your own copy

1. Download `strecke-template.xlsx` from this folder.
2. Open Google Drive, choose **New › File upload**, and pick the file.
3. Right-click the uploaded file and choose **Open with › Google Sheets**.
4. In Sheets, choose **File › Save as Google Sheets**. You now have a normal Google Sheet; the uploaded `.xlsx` can be deleted.

The other route: in any open spreadsheet, **File › Import › Upload**, then *Create new spreadsheet*. Google's help page "Use both Excel & Sheets: Best practices" (support.google.com/docs/answer/9331167) describes both.

Header notes and dropdowns (article, pos, source, verified) should survive the import, but Google does not promise this for every Excel feature (unverified for this file). If a dropdown is missing nothing breaks: the app reads free text tolerantly.

Then connect the sheet in the app, **Settings › Data**, following the numbered steps there. In short: **File › Share › Publish to web**, choose only the *Words* tab, choose **Comma-separated values (.csv)**, click **Publish**, and paste the link. Use a computer for this step; the menu wording may differ slightly. For the optional tabs, publish each one the same way and paste its link under *Optional tabs*: each tab has its own link.

**Publish only the tabs the app reads** (*Words*, and *Inbox* / *Meta* if you use them), never the entire document. Anyone with a published link can read that tab. You can stop publishing at any time from the same dialog.

If the link cannot be read on your phone, download the *Words* tab as CSV (**File › Download › Comma-separated values**) and pick the file in **Settings › Data › Or read a CSV file instead**. A file is not re-read by itself; pick a newer file to update.

## Already have a word list? Migrate without breaking anything

You do not need to start over, rename your tab, or use the template's column order.

1. **Make sure one column is called `word`** (or `Wort`, `German`, `Deutsch`, `Lemma`, `de`). That is the only required header.
2. **Name the meaning column** `meaning` (or `English`, `Bedeutung`, `Übersetzung`, `en`). Rows without a meaning are listed in the app and are not practised until filled.
3. **Add any other columns you want, anywhere**, with the names in [SHEET_SCHEMA.md](../SHEET_SCHEMA.md). Each one adds exercises. Columns the app does not know are ignored and listed once, so your own columns (notes, tags, colours) can stay.
4. **Optional tabs:** add a tab named `Inbox` with the headers `word`, `note`, `processed`, and a tab named `Meta` with `schema_version` and `1` in two cells. Missing tabs are fine.
5. **Progress stays attached when you edit rows.** Edits to the meaning, examples or any other column keep the word's history; so do a fixed typo in the word (up to two letters) and an article filled in later. If you expect to change the German word more than that, add an `id` column with any short unique text per row (1, 2, 3, … is fine).
6. Publish the words tab as CSV and connect it (above). The app lists, neutrally, any row it reads differently than you might expect ("Row 12 · Schrank: article missing"), with the spreadsheet's own row numbers. Fix those in the sheet whenever you like; they arrive on the next open.

The app is tolerant about:
- an article written in the word cell (`der Tisch`) or as `m` / `f` / `n`;
- German dates (`11.10.2026`);
- `source` written as `Claude`, `ChatGPT`, `AI`, `KI` or `ich`;
- `verified` written as `ja` / `nein`;
- empty cells, blank rows and a title row above the header.

The app never writes to the sheet: it only reads the published tabs.
